helps companies in the US and Europe hire experienced engineers & designers, from funded startups to teams like Klarna, Retool, and Pinterest. We’ve been doing this since 2015, and more than 1,500 companies have hired engineers through us.

New roles for Senior Designers come in all the time, and several are open right now.

Two ways to work with clients

  • Contract: most roles are contract-based. You join the client’s team and work as part of it.

  • Direct hire: some clients hire designers full-time, and we support you through the process.

Because companies trust our vetting, applying through is often a shortcut. You get to the client faster than going through their full hiring process on your own.

What you get

  • Competitive rate, based on your seniority and skills

  • We find the projects. No client hunting or rate negotiations. We match you manually based on your skills and preferences.

  • Flexible schedule. Work async or with a small overlap with the team’s hours.

  • No micromanagement, no screen trackers

  • Direct work with clients, most of them with technical backgrounds

  • Ongoing support from your application through every project, plus a community of engineers from 75+ countries

Who we’re looking for

Senior UI & UX Designers:

  • 5+ years of experience in UI & UX Design

  • 3+ years of commercial experience with Figma & 5+ years with Prototyping, OR 5+ years of commercial experience with Figma & 3+ years with Prototyping

  • Experience with Adobe is required

  • Experience in Product design is a must

Senior Graphic Designers:

  • 5+ years of experience in Graphic Design

  • 5+ years of commercial experience with Adobe Creative Suite & Adobe Illustrator

  • Strong design craft — as a Senior Designer, you're expected to build polished, production-ready work from scratch, with a solid grasp of design systems, component architecture, and how your decisions translate into real product or brand outcomes.

  • Clear and confident communication in English — advanced ability to discuss creative briefs, defend design decisions, and flag blockers early. Strong self-presentation is essential, particularly on client calls.

  • High ownership, zero hand-holding — you thrive working full-time remotely, manage your own time, and consistently hit deadlines without being chased.

  • Reliability — we need to trust you completely. If you commit to something, you deliver it. If something changes, you communicate early.

  • Fast ramp-up — you can absorb project context quickly, align with existing style guides or brand directions, and start producing valuable work within the first days, not weeks.

How it works

  1. Apply and complete your profile

  2. Verify your role

  3. Once approved, we match you with a project. Typical time to first project: 3 weeks

Ready? Apply and join the community.

Job Summary

We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to take on Koru's most ambiguous, highest-leverage design problems, the ones that span multiple client accounts, cross multiple teams, or don't have a defined brief yet. You'll set the standard for design quality and AI-informed practice across the accounts you touch, and operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where creating structure is part of the job, not something handed to you.

We're also looking for genuine fluency with AI in product design and not just familiarity with AI tools, but real judgement about when AI actually helps a user and when it quietly doesn't, backed by a track record of shipping AI-powered features responsibly, and comfort using AI tools as part of your own workflow, not just designing AI for others.

Key Responsibilities

Owning ambiguous, high-leverage work

  • Lead and ship large, cross-team or cross-account projects independently, often without a fully defined brief, adjusting scope as it changes rather than waiting for someone to hand you clarity.
  • Diagnose problems nobody has framed yet, spotting opportunities before they're assigned, not just executing what's already on the roadmap.
  • Set the quality bar and visual direction for an account or product line without personally executing every piece of it.
  • Apply deliberate leverage: know when a task is worth doing yourself versus building something, a pattern, a template, documentation, that helps everyone doing similar work after you.
  • Own design decisions across multiple surface areas or product lines at once where needed, not just a single feature in isolation.

Shaping how Koru designs with AI

  • Set AI UX standards for a client or product line, and build or maintain the pattern library and evaluation checklists other designers use.
  • Treat AI as a multiplier for your own design process, not a shortcut around it: use AI tools to speed up exploration and prototyping without letting them substitute for your own judgement.
  • Actively evolve Koru's own AI design practice as the field moves

Influence without authority

  • Build followership across teams through consistently clear thinking, not seniority or volume.
  • Mentor designers across projects, not just your own team, and act as a sponsor as well as a mentor, advocating for people in rooms they're not in, not just guiding them one to one.
  • Get Koru treated as a strategic partner through the calibre of your thinking as much as your output.

Contributing beyond the project

  • Lead initiatives that expand Koru's visibility or offerings
  • Extend and improve Koru's own internal design frameworks and processes, not just follow them.

Requirements

Experience

  • 8+ years of experience in product or UX design, the majority of it operating at a senior level or beyond.
  • A portfolio that shows genuine breadth of scope, not just polished screens, but measurable business outcomes and evidence of leading ambiguous, cross-functional work end to end. Strong enough to stand on its own without a verbal walkthrough.
  • Experience with B2B products and enterprise applications; HealthTech experience is a strong plus.
  • Real, hands-on experience designing AI-powered features or AI-native product ideas, not just using AI tools day to day. We'll ask you to speak to this specifically, ideally with a portfolio piece that shows it.
  • Comfortable prototyping in code, or close enough to front-end development to validate ideas without waiting on engineering.

Skills

  • Craft & judgement - deep design skill combined with the judgement to know when to apply it personally and when to build something that scales it to others.
  • AI fluency - genuine, applied understanding of AI capability and limitation in product design, not just enthusiasm for the space.
  • Influence without authority - a proven ability to set direction and raise the bar for people who don't report to you.
  • Business acumen - comfortable operating as a strategic partner to client leadership, not just a design resource.
  • Communication - able to make a case clearly enough that people who don't already agree with you can be moved.

Benefits

Why join us?

  • Own Koru's hardest, most ambiguous design problems, the ones that don't fit neatly inside one project or one team.
  • Shape how Koru designs with AI, for clients and internally, at a formative moment for the practice.
  • Be part of a collaborative, high-performance team that values your expertise and ideas.
  • Work remotely with flexibility, on meaningful, challenging work.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, portfolio, and a 5-minute introductory video. In the video, walk us through your most interesting project, where you are in your career right now, and what you're hoping to get out of your next role. We'd rather hear this in your own voice than read it in a cover letter.

About Sendmarc

We are a cyber security company that is on a mission to make the internet a safer place. We do this by delivering tooling and services related to an international standard, DMARC. Our technology enables organisations to protect their staff, customers, suppliers, and the whole world from email spoofing and impersonation attacks on their domains.

We’re a fully remote company with the majority of our builders working out of South Africa and sales teams in the Netherlands, the US, Latin America, Australia and the UK.

Why This Role Exists

The mission of this role is to create beautiful and user-friendly interfaces across Sendmarc’s digital products.

Sendmarc ships new capability fast, across a growing set of products and surfaces. This role exists to make sure every feature we ship is clear, consistent, and genuinely easy to use.

You’ll work alongside Sendmarc’s existing product design function, building out the design system that keeps our interfaces consistent as the product surface area grows, and working closely with Product and Engineering to take ideas from concept to shipped feature.

Outcomes

The core outcomes this role is accountable for:

End-to-End Product Design

Design and deliver product experiences that are intuitive, cohesive, and user-centric, communicating design thinking through wireframes, prototypes, sketches, user flows, mockups, and high-fidelity visual designs, and distilling complex problems into systematic, scalable solutions that get refined iteratively.

Usability & Research

Investigate usability pain points and apply UX heuristics to improve clarity and ease of use, and conduct research that informs design decisions, shapes product direction, and surfaces new opportunities.

Design System Ownership

Define, evolve, and maintain Sendmarc’s Design System, keeping the experience consistent and unified across the product ecosystem, and develop the usage guidelines, reusable components, content standards, and usability documentation that let product teams move faster.

Cross-Functional Delivery

Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Engineers, and stakeholders to plan, design, and implement new features, analysing business rules and technical constraints to keep solutions feasible, presenting design work and adjusting it based on feedback, and supporting engineers through delivery with assets, clarifications, and updates.

Competencies

PRODUCT DESIGN

  • Experience designing end-to-end product experiences, from wireframes and user flows through high-fidelity UI
  • Comfortable distilling complex problems into systematic, scalable design solutions, and refining them iteratively
  • Strong grounding in UX heuristics and usability principles, with a track record of removing friction and confusion from an interface

DESIGN SYSTEMS

  • Experience defining, evolving, and maintaining a design system: components, usage guidelines, content standards
  • Understands how a documented, reusable design system speeds up delivery for the wider product team

COLLABORATION & DELIVERY

  • Comfortable working closely with Product Managers, Engineers, and stakeholders to plan and ship new features
  • Able to translate business rules and technical constraints into feasible, effective design solutions
  • Confident presenting design work, gathering feedback, and iterating in response
  • Comfortable supporting engineers through delivery with assets, clarifications, and design updates

TOOLS & EXPERIENCE

  • Tertiary qualification in Design, Interaction Design, HCI, or a related discipline
  • 5+ years hands-on experience designing digital interfaces, preferably for SaaS or B2B products
  • Strong proficiency in Figma and prototyping tools
  • A portfolio demonstrating practical UX and UI design work

Who We're Looking For

You’re a practical, detail-oriented designer who gets real satisfaction from solving an interface problem cleanly and shipping something people find genuinely easy to use. You communicate design thinking clearly, through wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity mockups, and you’re comfortable working closely with Product and Engineering from early concept through to a shipped feature.

SaaS or B2B product experience is a plus, not a requirement: what matters more is a portfolio that shows sharp thinking and polished execution.

About the role

Hi, my name is Matt W, VP of Product & Design at Customer.io, and I'm looking for a Principal Product Designer. Principal Product Designer is the highest individual contributor design role at Customer.io. This person shapes the design vision for the company and influences how design is practiced here — through their own craft, through the standards their work sets, and through the partnerships they build with product and engineering leadership.

Customer.io is in a transformational moment: executing against a strong current product while redesigning what the product is and how it's experienced by a new generation of builders. This role has to straddle both — delivering quality and coherence in what exists today while driving the vision for where things go.

This is not a management role, but it's a leadership role in the fullest sense. Their influence is felt company-wide — in the product, in the culture, and in who we hire.

About you

You have a fully formed point of view on how AI changes what software means — for the people who use it, the people who build it, and the agents that increasingly operate it. Warp: We're Building the Platform for Agentic Development

Warp began with the vision of reimagining one of the fundamental dev tools, the terminal, to make it more usable and powerful for all developers. As AI has advanced, Warp has evolved beyond its terminal roots into a full agentic development environment: a workbench for dispatching agents to code, deploy, and debug production software.

Today, we have three products. Warp is the agentic development environment born out of the terminal, built on an orchestration platform for running hundreds of cloud agents in parallel. And Warp Factories is our newest product: infrastructure for engineering teams to build and run their own cloud software factories, where fleets of agents triage, spec, implement, review, and verify code across a company's entire SDLC. Together, these products are creating the scaffolding for developers to build their own workflows for working with agents.

In Warp, you can seamlessly switch between running commands, launching agents, and iterating on code with agents, eliminating the need to jump between a terminal and an IDE. It all works with our built in SOTA agent or top agents like Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode. On the orchestration side, you can build custom agents that are triggered programmatically, tracked centrally, and shared across full teams to run agents across organizations without compromising security or reliability. Continue a cloud agent run locally in Warp or on the web with one click. And with Warp Factories, teams can go a step further and set up entire automated workflows around their SDLC, retaining full control over their data, models, and compute along the way.

With over 1 million active developers at companies including Docker, Ramp, and Peloton, and over half of the Fortune 500, and revenue that grew over 44x last year, Warp is one of the fastest growing startups in the AI development space.

Our mission has remained the same even as AI has advanced: to empower developers to ship better software more quickly, freeing them to focus on the creative and rewarding aspects of their work. If you want to help define what development looks like in the agentic era at a company where your work reaches hundreds of thousands of engineers every day, we'd love to have you. For more information on our team and culture, we highly recommend reading our' How We Work' guide.

About Simulmedia

Since 2008, Simulmedia has helped brands and agencies turn TV into a measurable growth channel. Our AI-powered media platform for planning, activating, and measuring campaigns works across linear, local, and connected TV.

Everyone here owns problems end-to-end, and our design team is small, so your decisions ship and matter.

About the role

Think about it as a mix of a product manager's mindset with a strong design vertical skills. Design here is AI-first and builder-led. We expect you to take a problem, define ways to solve it, identify the best ways to shape the output, and involve stakeholders throughout the solution's development. Your output might be a Figma design mockup, a prototype, shipped production code, a PRD, or a decision document.

What you'll do

  • Own problems end to end. Define the problem with your PM and engineers, decide what should exist at all, explore options, validate them, and ship improvements that move key metrics. Stay with the work after handoff.
  • Work across the business. Client-facing products, internal tools, sales enablement, or customer experience, depending on priorities.
  • Start in writing. Use AI to clarify hypotheses, surface risks and edge cases, write short PRDs or decision documents. Sometimes the document is the final outcome: not every problem needs a UI solution.
  • Use research to go faster. Talk to sales managers, customer success managers, and internal users, run quick tests, and adjust direction based on what you learn. Use research to speed up decisions, not block them.
  • Prototype with AI. Build and iterate on flows in Claude Code, Cursor, or similar. AI writes the code, and you own structure, behavior, and UX quality.
  • UI Design. When it makes sense, turn validated concepts into production-ready designs with every state covered and aligned with our design system.
  • Ship with engineers. You'll occasionally ship small UI fixes to production; engineers own production code, and your share can grow over time.

What we expect from you

  • 3+ years as a product designer on complex B2B products with dense, data-heavy interfaces: tables, filters, reporting, multi-role flows.
  • A portfolio that shows product thinking, interaction design, and craft
  • At least several products you've built or prototyped in code with AI tools.
  • You proactively build domain and technical knowledge and get up to speed quickly on new problems.
  • Comfort in Claude Code, or similar: you can work in an existing codebase and get a prototype running without waiting for an engineer.
  • Good UI skills: your mockups are neat, balanced, and focused on user value.
  • Based anywhere in Ukraine
  • English at B2+ (upper-intermediate) or higher.

Nice to have

  • Ad tech, media, or analytics/reporting product experience.
  • A public GitHub or shipped side projects.
  • Experience in data visualization
  • Interest in growing your product management and engineering skills alongside design.

How we hire

Apply with a link to your portfolio. The process has three steps:

  1. Technical interview. Walk us through your portfolio and how you work: your research, how you prototype, and the decisions behind one project you built.
  2. Test task. We'd like to understand how you operate within an new domain and are ready to defend your own work
  3. Product manager interview. Product thinking and collaboration: how you define problems and success, prioritize, and work with a PM day to day.
